//1: VSCode-family editors (Cursor, Code OSS, Codium) — merge into .vscode/settings.json. Note: VSCode LSP extensions vary in how they accept a custom binary. The keys below cover rust-analyzer / pyright / typescript / gopls / sumneko-lua / ruby-lsp official extensions as of 2026-Q1. Replace /path/to/etzhayyim/root.
//2-pyright: Some pyright extensions ignore the override; in that case use the 'BasedPyright Configuration → Pyright Binary' setting or run attach-langserver.sh wrapped via a shim that adds 'python' as $1.
//3-lua: sumneko-lua extension accepts a custom binary only via the experimental 'Lua.misc.executablePath'; ymmv.
//4-caveat: For LSP extensions that DON'T expose a custom binary path, the only path forward is publishing a small VSCode extension that wraps the LSP with a custom transport. That extension is out of scope for L8 scaffold; add as 60-apps/etzhayyim-vscode-langserver/ when needed.
//5-args: Most VSCode LSP extensions pass a fixed args set to the binary. attach-langserver.sh accepts <lang> as $1 but also reads $ETZHAYYIM_LANG_FALLBACK from env. If the extension swallows args, create a one-line shim: #!/bin/sh\nexec /path/to/attach-langserver.sh rust "$@"
